sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region between the curve and the x-axis. \(\displaystyle y=27-3\left(x+1\right)^{2},\qquad -4\le x\le 2\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Check the sign. The parabola opens down and meets the x-axis at \(x=-4\) and \(x=2\); between them it is above the axis. Integrate. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{-4}^{2}\left(27-3\left(x+1\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{-4}^{2}\left(-3x^{2} - 6x + 24\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 24x\right]_{-4}^{2}\) \(\displaystyle =108\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region between the curve and the x-axis. \(\displaystyle y=2\sqrt{x},\qquad 0\le x\le 1\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Check the sign. \(2\sqrt{x}\ge 0\) for \(x\ge 0\). Integrate. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{1}2\sqrt{x}\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{1}2\sqrt{x}\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[\frac{4x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{4}{3}\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region between the curve and the line. \(\displaystyle y=4\sin x,\qquad y=0,\qquad 0\le x\le \pi\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Subtract the line. The vertical distance between the curve and \(y=0\) is \(4\sin x\), which is never negative on the interval. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{\pi}4\sin x\,dx=\left[-4\cos x\right]_{0}^{\pi}=4+4=8\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator A curve lies above the x-axis on the interval shown. \(\displaystyle y=4\sqrt{16-x^{2}},\quad -4\le x\le 4\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Recognize the shape. The graph of \(y=\sqrt{16-x^{2}}\) is the upper half of the circle of radius 4; multiplying by 4 stretches it vertically, which multiplies the area by 4. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{-4}^{4}4\sqrt{16-x^{2}}\,dx=4\cdot\frac{1}{2}\pi(4)^{2}=32\pi\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region between the curve and the x-axis. \(\displaystyle y=x^{2} + 1,\qquad 0\le x\le 3\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Check the sign. \(x^{2} + 1\ge 0\) on \([0,3]\). Integrate. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{3}\left(x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{3}\left(x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[\frac{x^{3}}{3} + x\right]_{0}^{3}\) \(\displaystyle =12\)

Split the interval at \(x=-\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x=1\). The area counts every region as positive, but \(\int f(x)\,dx\) is negative where the curve is below the x-axis, so one integral of \(f\) over the whole interval would subtract those regions instead of adding them. sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region enclosed by the curves. \(\displaystyle y=\frac{2}{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=3-x\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curves.
parts.explanation: Find where the curves meet. \(\frac{2}{x}=3-x\) gives \(x^{2}-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2)=0\), so \(x=1\) and \(x=2\). Between them the line is above the curve (at \(x=1.5\): \(1.5\gt \frac{4}{3}\)). Integrate. An antiderivative of \(3-x-\frac{2}{x}\) is \(3x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}-2\ln x\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{1}^{2}\left(3-x-\frac{2}{x}\right)dx=\left[3x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}-2\ln x\right]_{1}^{2}=\frac{3}{2} - 2\ln 2\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region between the curves from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\). \(\displaystyle y=e^{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=x+1\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Decide which is on top. The tangent line \(y=x+1\) lies below \(y=e^{x}\) (they touch at \(x=0\)). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{1}\left(e^{x}-(x+1)\right)dx=\left[e^{x}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x\right]_{0}^{1}=\left(e-\frac{3}{2}\right)-1=e - \frac{5}{2}\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=e^{x}\), \(y=e^{-x}\) and the line \(x=\ln 3\). \(\displaystyle y=e^{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=e^{-x}\) \(\displaystyle x=\ln 3\)

parts.prompt: Find the area.
parts.explanation: Find where the curves meet and which is on top. \(e^{x}=e^{-x}\) at \(x=0\); for \(x\gt 0\), \(e^{x}\gt 1\gt e^{-x}\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{\ln 3}\left(e^{x}-e^{-x}\right)dx\) Evaluate. An antiderivative is \(e^{x}+e^{-x}\); \(e^{\ln 3}=3\) and \(e^{-\ln 3}=\frac{1}{3}\). \(\displaystyle A=\left(3+\frac{1}{3}\right)-(1+1)=\frac{4}{3}\)

[figure] \(y=\sqrt{x}\) \(y=x-12\) one slice (length \(s\)) [figure] One cross section: a rectangle with base \(s\) and height \(3s\); \(A=3s^{2}\) Find the bounds. \(\sqrt{x}=x-12\) at \(x=16\) (then \(y=4\)); the line meets the x-axis at \(x=12\). In terms of y the left boundary is \(x=y^{2}\) and the right boundary is \(x=y+12\), for \(0\le y\le 4\). Choose the slices. Cross sections are perpendicular to the x-axis, so integrate with respect to \(x\). Each slice is vertical; its length across the region is top minus bottom, \(s(x)\). Split the integral at \(x=12\). At \(x=12\), \(y=x - 12\) meets the x-axis, \(y=0\): \(x - 12=0\) when \(x=12\). Before \(x=12\) the lower boundary of the region is the x-axis, \(y=0\); after it, the lower boundary is \(y=x - 12\). The upper boundary, \(y=\sqrt{x}\), is the same on both sides. Because the lower boundary changes, the slice length \(s(x)\) has a different formula on each side of \(x=12\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x=12\), with one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle s(x)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{x}, & 0\le x\le 12\\\sqrt{x}-\left(x - 12\right), & 12\le x\le 16\end{cases}\) Find the area of one cross section. The base is \(s\) and the height is \(3s\), so the area is \(3s^{2}\). On each piece, \(A(x)=3\left(s(x)\right)^{2}\), with the slice length \(s(x)\) of that piece. Set up the volume. Integrate the cross-sectional area over each piece and add the results. \(\displaystyle V=3\int_{0}^{12}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{2}\,dx + 3\int_{12}^{16}\left(\sqrt{x}-\left(x - 12\right)\right)^{2}\,dx\)

parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a disk: its radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the boundary. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=-\frac{x}{2} + 1\) axis of rotation \(y=0\) radius \(R\) [figure] One disk, face on: area \(\pi R^{2}\) Find the bounds. The slanted side is \(y=-\frac{x}{2} + 1\), or solved for x, \(x=-2y + 2\); x runs from 0 to 2 and y from 0 to 1. Choose the slices. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are disks of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis: \(R(x)=1 - \frac{x}{2}\). Set up the volume. Each disk has area \(\pi R^{2}\). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{2}\left(1 - \frac{x}{2}\right)^{2}\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \pi\int_{0}^{2}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{4} - x + 1\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\pi\left[\frac{x^{3}}{12} - \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x\right]_{0}^{2}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{2}{3}\pi\)

The left boundary, \(x=2\), is the same on both sides. Because the right boundary changes, the outer radius \(R(y)\) has a different formula on each side of \(y=1\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(y=1\), with one integral for each piece. \(r(y)=2\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle R(y)=\begin{cases}4, & 0\le y\le 1\\\frac{4}{y}, & 1\le y\le 2\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. The axis \(y=-3\) is horizontal, so the shells are horizontal: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dy\), and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(y)=3 + y\). The height is right minus left: \(h(y)=1-y^{2}\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(3 + y\right)\left(1-y^{2}\right)\,dy\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle 2\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(-y^{3} - 3y^{2} + y + 3\right)\,dy\) \(\displaystyle =2\pi\left[-\frac{y^{4}}{4} - y^{3} + \frac{y^{2}}{2} + 3y\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{9}{2}\pi\)

leaks.note: That is the height of the shell; the radius is the distance from the axis.

Each slice parallel to the axis sweeps out a cylindrical shell: its radius \(r\) is the distance from the axis to the slice, and its height \(h\) is the length of the slice. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=-2x + 4\) axis of rotation \(y=0\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell, on its side: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Choose the shells. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so the shells are horizontal: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dy\), and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(y)=y\). The height is right minus left: \(h(y)=-\frac{y}{2} + 2\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{4}y\left(-\frac{y}{2} + 2\right)\,dy\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is revolved about the x-axis.
parts.explanation: Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle 2\pi\int_{0}^{4}\left(-\frac{y^{2}}{2} + 2y\right)\,dy\) \(\displaystyle =2\pi\left[-\frac{y^{3}}{6} + y^{2}\right]_{0}^{4}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{32}{3}\pi\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the x-axis. Using washers, write an integral expression for the volume.
parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=x^{2}\) \(y=x^{3}\) axis of rotation \(y=0\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Choose the slices. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=x^{2}\) and \(r(x)=x^{3}\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(\left(x^{2}\right)^{2}-\left(x^{3}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\)

parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=\sqrt{x}\) \(x=4\) axis of rotation \(y=-1\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Choose the slices. The axis \(y=-1\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(-1\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=1 + \sqrt{x}\) and \(r(x)=1\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{4}\left(\left(1 + \sqrt{x}\right)^{2}-1^{2}\right)\,dx\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the y-axis. Using cylindrical shells, write an integral expression for the volume.
parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice parallel to the axis sweeps out a cylindrical shell: its radius \(r\) is the distance from the axis to the slice, and its height \(h\) is the length of the slice. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=\sqrt{x}\) \(x=4\) axis of rotation \(x=0\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Choose the shells. The axis \(x=0\) is vertical, so the shells are vertical: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dx\). Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=x\). The height is top minus bottom: \(h(x)=\sqrt{x}\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{4}x\sqrt{x}\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is revolved about the y-axis.
parts.explanation: Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle 2\pi\int_{0}^{4}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =2\pi\left[\frac{2x^{\frac{5}{2}}}{5}\right]_{0}^{4}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{128}{5}\pi\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the triangular region with vertices \((0,0)\), \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\). Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=-x + 1\) \(\displaystyle x=0\) \(\displaystyle y=0\)

Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=e^{2x}\) \(x=1\) axis of rotation \(y=8\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Find the bounds. x runs from 0 to 1; the curve rises from \(y=1\) to \(y=e^{2}\). Below \(y=1\) the region is a rectangle; above it the left boundary is \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\). Choose the slices. The axis \(y=8\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies below the axis, so each radius is \(8\) minus a boundary height. The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=8\) and \(r(x)=8-e^{2x}\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(8^{2}-\left(8-e^{2x}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(8^{2}-\left(8-e^{2x}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\approx 118.479\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the line \(x=3\). Find the volume of this solid. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=e^{2x}\) \(x=1\) axis of rotation \(x=3\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Choose the slices. The axis \(x=3\) is vertical, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dy\), and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies to the left of the axis, so each radius is \(3\) minus a boundary x-value. The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one. Split the integral at \(y=1\). At \(y=1\), \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\) meets the y-axis, \(x=0\): \(\frac{\ln y}{2}=0\) when \(y=1\). Below \(y=1\) the left boundary of the region is the y-axis, \(x=0\); above it, the left boundary is \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\). The right boundary, \(x=1\), is the same on both sides. Because the left boundary changes, the outer radius \(R(y)\) has a different formula on each side of \(y=1\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(y=1\), with one integral for each piece. \(r(y)=2\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle R(y)=\begin{cases}3, & 0\le y\le 1\\3-\frac{\ln y}{2}, & 1\le y\le e^{2}\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(3^{2}-2^{2}\right)\,dy + \pi\int_{1}^{e^{2}}\left(\left(3-\frac{\ln y}{2}\right)^{2}-2^{2}\right)\,dy\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(3^{2}-2^{2}\right)\,dy + \pi\int_{1}^{e^{2}}\left(\left(3-\frac{\ln y}{2}\right)^{2}-2^{2}\right)\,dy\approx 47.038\)

Each slice parallel to the axis sweeps out a cylindrical shell: its radius \(r\) is the distance from the axis to the slice, and its height \(h\) is the length of the slice. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=2\cos x\) \(y=3x^{2}\) axis of rotation \(x=3\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Choose the shells. The axis \(x=3\) is vertical, so the shells are vertical: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dx\). Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=3 - x\). The height is top minus bottom: \(h(x)=2\cos x-3x^{2}\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{-0.711}^{0.711}\left(3 - x\right)\left(2\cos x-3x^{2}\right)\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid in Part B. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{-0.711}^{0.711}\left(3 - x\right)\left(2\cos x-3x^{2}\right)\,dx\approx 35.654\)

One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=e^{2x}\) \(x=1\) axis of rotation \(y=8\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell, on its side: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Find the bounds. x runs from 0 to 1; the curve rises from \(y=1\) to \(y=e^{2}\). Below \(y=1\) the region is a rectangle; above it the left boundary is \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\). Choose the shells. The axis \(y=8\) is horizontal, so the shells are horizontal: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dy\), and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(y)=8 - y\). The height is right minus left, \(h(y)\). Split the integral at \(y=1\). At \(y=1\), \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\) meets the y-axis, \(x=0\): \(\frac{\ln y}{2}=0\) when \(y=1\). Below \(y=1\) the left boundary of the region is the y-axis, \(x=0\); above it, the left boundary is \(x=\frac{\ln y}{2}\). The right boundary, \(x=1\), is the same on both sides. Because the left boundary changes, the shell height \(h(y)\) has a different formula on each side of \(y=1\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(y=1\), with one integral for each piece. \(r(y)=8 - y\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle h(y)=\begin{cases}1, & 0\le y\le 1\\1-\frac{\ln y}{2}, & 1\le y\le e^{2}\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(8 - y\right)\,dy + 2\pi\int_{1}^{e^{2}}\left(8 - y\right)\left(1-\frac{\ln y}{2}\right)\,dy\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(8 - y\right)\,dy + 2\pi\int_{1}^{e^{2}}\left(8 - y\right)\left(1-\frac{\ln y}{2}\right)\,dy\approx 118.479\)

parts.explanation: Region R and the axis of rotation. Compare it with the region on your calculator graph. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=2\cos x\) \(y=2x^{2}\) axis of rotation \(y=3\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Find the bounds. With a calculator, \(2\cos x=2x^{2}\) at \(x\approx\pm0.8241\). Choose the slices. The axis \(y=3\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies below the axis, so each radius is \(3\) minus a boundary height. The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=3-2x^{2}\) and \(r(x)=3-2\cos x\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{-0.824}^{0.824}\left(\left(3-2x^{2}\right)^{2}-\left(3-2\cos x\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{-0.824}^{0.824}\left(\left(3-2x^{2}\right)^{2}-\left(3-2\cos x\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\approx 26.562\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the line \(x=3\). Write an integral expression for the volume of this solid (use cylindrical shells). You may use decimal limits.
parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice parallel to the axis sweeps out a cylindrical shell: its radius \(r\) is the distance from the axis to the slice, and its height \(h\) is the length of the slice. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=2\cos x\) \(y=2x^{2}\) axis of rotation \(x=3\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Choose the shells. The axis \(x=3\) is vertical, so the shells are vertical: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dx\). Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=3 - x\). The height is top minus bottom: \(h(x)=2\cos x-2x^{2}\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{-0.824}^{0.824}\left(3 - x\right)\left(2\cos x-2x^{2}\right)\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid in Part B. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{-0.824}^{0.824}\left(3 - x\right)\left(2\cos x-2x^{2}\right)\,dx\approx 41.271\)

sequenceCatalog.question: Calculator active Let \(R\) be the region enclosed by the x-axis, the y-axis, \(x=1\) and \(y=e^{x}\). Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=e^{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=0\) \(\displaystyle x=0\) \(\displaystyle x=1\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the x-axis. Find the volume of the solid. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: Region R and the axis of rotation. Compare it with the region on your calculator graph. Each slice parallel to the axis sweeps out a cylindrical shell: its radius \(r\) is the distance from the axis to the slice, and its height \(h\) is the length of the slice. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=e^{x}\) \(x=1\) axis of rotation \(y=0\) shell height \(h\) shell radius \(r\) [figure] One shell, on its side: volume \(2\pi r h\) times its thickness Find the bounds. x runs from 0 to 1; the curve rises from \(y=1\) to \(y=e\). Below \(y=1\) the region is a rectangle; above it the left boundary is \(x=\ln y\). Choose the shells. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so the shells are horizontal: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dy\), and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(y)=y\). The height is right minus left, \(h(y)\). Split the integral at \(y=1\). At \(y=1\), \(x=\ln y\) meets the y-axis, \(x=0\): \(\ln y=0\) when \(y=1\). Below \(y=1\) the left boundary of the region is the y-axis, \(x=0\); above it, the left boundary is \(x=\ln y\). The right boundary, \(x=1\), is the same on both sides. Because the left boundary changes, the shell height \(h(y)\) has a different formula on each side of \(y=1\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(y=1\), with one integral for each piece. \(r(y)=y\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle h(y)=\begin{cases}1, & 0\le y\le 1\\1-\ln y, & 1\le y\le e\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}y\,dy + 2\pi\int_{1}^{e}y\left(1-\ln y\right)\,dy\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}y\,dy + 2\pi\int_{1}^{e}y\left(1-\ln y\right)\,dy\approx 10.036\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is revolved about the y-axis. Write an integral expression for the volume of this solid. You may use decimal limits.
parts.explanation: The region, the axis and one slice. Each slice perpendicular to the axis sweeps out a washer: the outer radius \(R\) runs from the axis to the farther boundary, the inner radius \(r\) to the nearer one. One slice is drawn on the graph; the second picture shows what it sweeps out. [figure] \(y=e^{x}\) \(x=1\) axis of rotation \(x=0\) outer radius \(R\) inner radius \(r\) [figure] One washer, face on: area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) Choose the slices. The axis \(x=0\) is vertical, so slice perpendicular to it with thickness \(dy\): the slices are disks where the region touches the axis and washers where it does not, and every boundary is written as x in terms of y. Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies to the right of the axis, so each radius is a boundary x-value minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one. Split the integral at \(y=1\). At \(y=1\), \(x=\ln y\) meets the y-axis, \(x=0\): \(\ln y=0\) when \(y=1\). Below \(y=1\) the left boundary of the region is the y-axis, \(x=0\); above it, the left boundary is \(x=\ln y\). The right boundary, \(x=1\), is the same on both sides. Because the left boundary changes, the inner radius \(r(y)\) has a different formula on each side of \(y=1\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(y=1\), with one integral for each piece. \(R(y)=1\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle r(y)=\begin{cases}0, & 0\le y\le 1\\\ln y, & 1\le y\le e\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each slice has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting); a disk is the case \(r=0\). Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}1^{2}\,dy + \pi\int_{1}^{e}\left(1^{2}-\left(\ln y\right)^{2}\right)\,dy\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid in Part B. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}1^{2}\,dy + \pi\int_{1}^{e}\left(1^{2}-\left(\ln y\right)^{2}\right)\,dy\approx 6.283\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the region enclosed by \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and \(y=x^{3}\), as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=\sqrt{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=x^{3}\) [figure] \(y=\sqrt{x}\) \(y=x^{3}\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. Set \(\sqrt{x}=x^{3}\): the curves meet at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) (where \(y=1\)). Set up the area with vertical slices. Use vertical slices of width \(dx\): each has height top minus bottom. From \(x=0\) to \(x=1\) the top is \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and the bottom is \(y=x^{3}\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt{x}-x^{3}\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{1}\left(-x^{3} + \sqrt{x}\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-\frac{x^{4}}{4} + \frac{2x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{5}{12}\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is the base of a solid. Cross sections of the solid perpendicular to the y-axis are isosceles right triangles with one leg across the region. Find the volume of the solid.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. Cross sections are perpendicular to the y-axis, so integrate with respect to \(y\). Each slice is horizontal; its length across the region is right minus left: \(s(y)=\sqrt[3]{y}-y^{2}\). Find the area of one cross section. An isosceles right triangle with legs \(s\) has area \(\frac{1}{2}s^{2}\). So \(A(y)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt[3]{y}-y^{2}\right)^{2}\). Set up the volume. Add the cross sections: integrate their area. \(\displaystyle V=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt[3]{y}-y^{2}\right)^{2}\,dy\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\left(y^{4} - 2y^{\frac{7}{3}} + y^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)\,dy\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{y^{5}}{5} - \frac{3y^{\frac{10}{3}}}{5} + \frac{3y^{\frac{5}{3}}}{5}\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{1}{10}\)

parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the x-axis.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are washers of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=\sqrt{x}\) and \(r(x)=x^{3}\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{2}-\left(x^{3}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the region bounded by the line \(y=1\), the curve \(y=x^{2}\) and the y-axis, as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=1\) \(\displaystyle y=x^{2}\) \(\displaystyle x=0\) [figure] \(y=x^{2}\) \(y=1\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. \(x^{2}=1\) at \(x=1\). Solved for x, the curve is \(x=\sqrt{y}\), and y runs from 0 to 1. Set up the area with vertical slices. Use vertical slices of width \(dx\): each has height top minus bottom. From \(x=0\) to \(x=1\) the top is \(y=1\) and the bottom is \(y=x^{2}\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{1}\left(1-x^{2}\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{1}\left(-x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-\frac{x^{3}}{3} + x\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{2}{3}\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is the base of a solid. Cross sections of the solid perpendicular to the x-axis are semicircles whose diameter lies across the region. Find the volume of the solid.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. Cross sections are perpendicular to the x-axis, so integrate with respect to \(x\). Each slice is vertical; its length across the region is top minus bottom: \(s(x)=1-x^{2}\). Find the area of one cross section. The slice across the region is the diameter of the semicircle: \(d=s\). So its radius is \(r=\frac{s}{2}\), and its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^{2}=\frac{\pi}{8}s^{2}\). So \(A(x)=\frac{\pi}{8}\left(1-x^{2}\right)^{2}\). Set up the volume. Add the cross sections: integrate their area. \(\displaystyle V=\frac{\pi}{8}\int_{0}^{1}\left(1-x^{2}\right)^{2}\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{8}\int_{0}^{1}\left(x^{4} - 2x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{\pi}{8}\left[\frac{x^{5}}{5} - \frac{2x^{3}}{3} + x\right]_{0}^{1}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{1}{15}\pi\)

parts.prompt: Using cylindrical shells, write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the line \(x=3\).

Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(3 - x\right)\left(1-x^{2}\right)\,dx\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the region bounded by \(y=3x\), \(y=2x\) and \(x=2\), as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=3x\) \(\displaystyle y=2x\) \(\displaystyle x=2\) [figure] \(y=3x\) \(y=2x\) \(x=2\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. The lines meet at the origin and reach \(x=2\) at \(y=4\) and \(y=6\). With horizontal slices the right boundary is \(x=\frac{y}{2}\) up to \(y=4\) and \(x=2\) above it. Set up the area with vertical slices. Use vertical slices of width \(dx\): each has height top minus bottom. From \(x=0\) to \(x=2\) the top is \(y=3x\) and the bottom is \(y=2x\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{2}\left(3x-2x\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. So its area is \(\frac{1}{4}\pi r^{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}s^{2}\). So \(A(x)=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(3x-2x\right)^{2}\). Set up the volume. Add the cross sections: integrate their area. \(\displaystyle V=\frac{\pi}{4}\int_{0}^{2}\left(3x-2x\right)^{2}\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{4}\int_{0}^{2}x^{2}\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{\pi}{4}\left[\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{2}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{2}{3}\pi\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the triangular region with vertices \((0,0)\), \((2,0)\) and \((0,3)\), as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=-\frac{3x}{2} + 3\) \(\displaystyle x=0\) \(\displaystyle y=0\) [figure] \(y=-\frac{3x}{2} + 3\)

parts.explanation: Find the bounds. Set \(y^{2}=2y + 8\): \(y^{2}-2y-8=(y-4)(y+2)=0\), so \(y=-2\) and \(y=4\) (the points \((4,-2)\) and \((16,4)\)). Solved for y, the line is \(y=\frac{x}{2} - 4\). Set up the area with horizontal slices. Use horizontal slices of height \(dy\): each has length right minus left. From \(y=-2\) to \(y=4\) the right side is \(x=2y + 8\) and the left side is \(x=y^{2}\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{-2}^{4}\left(2y + 8-y^{2}\right)\,dy\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{4}\left(-y^{2} + 2y + 8\right)\,dy\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-\frac{y^{3}}{3} + y^{2} + 8y\right]_{-2}^{4}\) \(\displaystyle =36\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is the base of a solid. Cross sections of the solid perpendicular to the x-axis are semicircles whose diameter lies across the region. Find the volume of the solid.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. Cross sections are perpendicular to the x-axis, so integrate with respect to \(x\). Each slice is vertical; its length across the region is top minus bottom, \(s(x)\). Split the integral at \(x=4\). At \(x=4\), \(y=\frac{x}{2} - 4\) meets \(y=-\sqrt{x}\): \(\frac{x}{2} - 4=-\sqrt{x}\) when \(x=4\). Before \(x=4\) the lower boundary of the region is \(y=-\sqrt{x}\); after it, the lower boundary is \(y=\frac{x}{2} - 4\). The upper boundary, \(y=\sqrt{x}\), is the same on both sides. Because the lower boundary changes, the slice length \(s(x)\) has a different formula on each side of \(x=4\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x=4\), with one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle s(x)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{x}-\left(-\sqrt{x}\right), & 0\le x\le 4\\\sqrt{x}-\left(\frac{x}{2} - 4\right), & 4\le x\le 16\end{cases}\) Find the area of one cross section. The slice across the region is the diameter of the semicircle: \(d=s\). So its radius is \(r=\frac{s}{2}\), and its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^{2}=\frac{\pi}{8}s^{2}\). On each piece, \(A(x)=\frac{\pi}{8}\left(s(x)\right)^{2}\), with the slice length \(s(x)\) of that piece. Set up the volume. Integrate the cross-sectional area over each piece and add the results. \(\displaystyle V=\frac{\pi}{8}\int_{0}^{4}\left(\sqrt{x}-\left(-\sqrt{x}\right)\right)^{2}\,dx + \frac{\pi}{8}\int_{4}^{16}\left(\sqrt{x}-\left(\frac{x}{2} - 4\right)\right)^{2}\,dx\) Evaluate. Evaluate each integral and add the results. \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{8}\int_{0}^{4}4x\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{\pi}{8}\left[2x^{2}\right]_{0}^{4}\) \(\displaystyle =4\pi\) \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{8}\int_{4}^{16}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{4} - x^{\frac{3}{2}} - 3x + 8\sqrt{x} + 16\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{\pi}{8}\left[\frac{x^{3}}{12} - \frac{2x^{\frac{5}{2}}}{5} - \frac{3x^{2}}{2} + \frac{16x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3} + 16x\right]_{4}^{16}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{131}{15}\pi\) \(\displaystyle \text{Total}=\frac{191}{15}\pi\)

The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=2 + x\). The height is top minus bottom, \(h(x)\). Split the integral at \(x=4\). At \(x=4\), \(y=\frac{x}{2} - 4\) meets \(y=-\sqrt{x}\): \(\frac{x}{2} - 4=-\sqrt{x}\) when \(x=4\). Because the lower boundary changes, the shell height \(h(x)\) has a different formula on each side of \(x=4\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x=4\), with one integral for each piece. \(r(x)=2 + x\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle h(x)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{x}-\left(-\sqrt{x}\right), & 0\le x\le 4\\\sqrt{x}-\left(\frac{x}{2} - 4\right), & 4\le x\le 16\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0}^{4}\left(2 + x\right)\left(\sqrt{x}-\left(-\sqrt{x}\right)\right)\,dx + 2\pi\int_{4}^{16}\left(2 + x\right)\left(\sqrt{x}-\left(\frac{x}{2} - 4\right)\right)\,dx\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the region enclosed by \(y=-x^{2} + 9\) and the x-axis, as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=-x^{2} + 9\) \(\displaystyle y=0\) [figure] \(y=-x^{2} + 9\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. \(-x^{2} + 9=0\) at \(x=\pm 3\); the top of the region is \(y=9\). Solved for x, \(x=\pm\sqrt{9-y}\). Set up the area with vertical slices. Use vertical slices of width \(dx\): each has height top minus bottom. From \(x=-3\) to \(x=3\) the top is \(y=-x^{2} + 9\) and the bottom is \(y=0\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{-3}^{3}\left(-x^{2} + 9\right)\,dx\) Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{-3}^{3}\left(-x^{2} + 9\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-\frac{x^{3}}{3} + 9x\right]_{-3}^{3}\) \(\displaystyle =36\)

parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the x-axis.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it: the slices are disks of thickness \(dx\). Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis: \(R(x)=9 - x^{2}\). Set up the volume. Each disk has area \(\pi R^{2}\). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{-3}^{3}\left(9 - x^{2}\right)^{2}\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Using cylindrical shells, write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the line \(x=-4\).
parts.explanation: Choose the shells. The axis \(x=-4\) is vertical, so the shells are vertical: slice parallel to the axis with thickness \(dx\). Find the radius and height. The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=4 + x\). The height is top minus bottom: \(h(x)=-x^{2} + 9\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{-3}^{3}\left(4 + x\right)\left(-x^{2} + 9\right)\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the line \(x=-4\).
parts.explanation: Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle 2\pi\int_{-3}^{3}\left(-x^{3} - 4x^{2} + 9x + 36\right)\,dx\) \(\displaystyle =2\pi\left[-\frac{x^{4}}{4} - \frac{4x^{3}}{3} + \frac{9x^{2}}{2} + 36x\right]_{-3}^{3}\) \(\displaystyle =288\pi\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(R\) be the region in the first quadrant bounded above by \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and below by the x-axis and the line \(y=x-6\), as shown in the figure. Answer each part. \(\displaystyle y=\sqrt{x}\) \(\displaystyle y=x-6\) \(\displaystyle y=0\) [figure] \(y=\sqrt{x}\) \(y=x-6\)

parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, a single integral in terms of \(y\) for the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. \(\sqrt{x}=x-6\) at \(x=9\) (then \(y=3\)); the line meets the x-axis at \(x=6\). In terms of y the left boundary is \(x=y^{2}\) and the right boundary is \(x=y+6\), for \(0\le y\le 3\). Set up the area with horizontal slices. Use horizontal slices of height \(dy\): each has length right minus left. From \(y=0\) to \(y=3\) the right side is \(x=y + 6\) and the left side is \(x=y^{2}\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{3}\left(y + 6-y^{2}\right)\,dy\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Evaluate. Expand the integrand, find an antiderivative and evaluate it at the limits. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{3}\left(-y^{2} + y + 6\right)\,dy\) \(\displaystyle =\left[-\frac{y^{3}}{3} + \frac{y^{2}}{2} + 6y\right]_{0}^{3}\) \(\displaystyle =\frac{27}{2}\)

parts.prompt: \(R\) is the base of a solid. Cross sections of the solid perpendicular to the y-axis are rectangles whose height is twice the base across the region. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. Cross sections are perpendicular to the y-axis, so integrate with respect to \(y\). Each slice is horizontal; its length across the region is right minus left: \(s(y)=y + 6-y^{2}\). Find the area of one cross section. The base is \(s\) and the height is \(2s\), so the area is \(2s^{2}\). So \(A(y)=2\left(y + 6-y^{2}\right)^{2}\). Set up the volume. Add the cross sections: integrate their area. \(\displaystyle V=2\int_{0}^{3}\left(y + 6-y^{2}\right)^{2}\,dy\)

parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the x-axis.
parts.explanation: Choose the slices. The axis \(y=0\) is horizontal, so slice perpendicular to it with thickness \(dx\): the slices are disks where the region touches the axis and washers where it does not. Measure the radii from the axis. The region lies above the axis, so each radius is a boundary height minus \(0\). The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one. Split the integral at \(x=6\). At \(x=6\), \(y=x - 6\) meets the x-axis, \(y=0\): \(x - 6=0\) when \(x=6\). Before \(x=6\) the lower boundary of the region is the x-axis, \(y=0\); after it, the lower boundary is \(y=x - 6\). The upper boundary, \(y=\sqrt{x}\), is the same on both sides. Because the lower boundary changes, the inner radius \(r(x)\) has a different formula on each side of \(x=6\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x=6\), with one integral for each piece. \(R(x)=\sqrt{x}\) on the whole interval. \(\displaystyle r(x)=\begin{cases}0, & 0\le x\le 6\\x - 6, & 6\le x\le 9\end{cases}\) Set up the volume. Each slice has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting); a disk is the case \(r=0\). Write one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{0}^{6}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{2}\,dx + \pi\int_{6}^{9}\left(\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{2}-\left(x - 6\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator Let \(f\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}\). Let \(R\) be the region bounded by the graph of \(f\) and the horizontal line \(y=1\), as shown in the figure. Answer each part. [figure] \(y=\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}\) \(y=1\)

parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.explanation: Find where the curve meets the line. \(\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}=1\) gives \(1+x^{2}=4\), so \(x^{2}=3\) and \(x=\pm \sqrt{3}\). Set up and evaluate the area. On \(\left[-\sqrt{3},\sqrt{3}\right]\) the curve is above the line. An antiderivative of \(\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}\) is \(4\tan^{-1}x\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}-1\right)dx\) \(\displaystyle =\left[4\tan^{-1}x-x\right]_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\) \(\displaystyle =2\left(4\cdot\frac{\pi}{3}-1\cdot \sqrt{3}\right)=\frac{8}{3}\pi - 2\sqrt{3}\)

The region lies below the axis, so each radius is \(4\) minus a boundary height. The outer radius R reaches the boundary farther from the axis; the inner radius r reaches the nearer one: \(R(x)=3\) and \(r(x)=4-\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}\). Set up the volume. Each washer has area \(\pi\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\) (square each radius before subtracting). \(\displaystyle V=\pi\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left(3^{2}-\left(4-\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx\)

parts.prompt: Let \(h(x)\) be the vertical distance between the point \((x,f(x))\) and the line \(y=1\). Find the rate of change of \(h(x)\) with respect to \(x\) at \(x=-1\).
parts.explanation: Write h(x) without absolute values. At \(x=-1\), which lies between \(-\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{3}\), the curve is above the line, so \(h(x)=f(x)-1\) and \(h'(x)=f'(x)\). Differentiate. \(f(x)=4\left(1+x^{2}\right)^{-1}\), so \(f'(x)=-\frac{8x}{\left(1+x^{2}\right)^{2}}\). \(\displaystyle f'\left(-1\right)=2\) \(\displaystyle h'\left(-1\right)=2\)

Split the integral at \(x\approx 0.812\). At \(x\approx 0.812\), \(y=2-x\) meets \(y=2\ln\left(x+1\right)\): \(2-x=2\ln\left(x+1\right)\) when \(x\approx 0.812\) (calculator). Before \(x\approx 0.812\) the upper boundary of the region is \(y=2\ln\left(x+1\right)\); after it, the upper boundary is \(y=2-x\). The lower boundary, the x-axis, \(y=0\), is the same on both sides. Because the upper boundary changes, the height of a slice, \(h(x)\), has a different formula on each side of \(x\approx 0.812\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x\approx 0.812\), with one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle h(x)=\begin{cases}2\ln\left(x+1\right), & 0\le x\le 0.812\\2-x, & 0.812\le x\le 2\end{cases}\) Write one integral for each piece. parts.prompt: Find the area of the region. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.explanation: Find the bounds. The curve meets the x-axis at \(x=0\) and the line at \(x=b\approx3.4967\) (calculator), where \(y\approx1.5033\); the line meets the x-axis at \(x=5\). Solved for x: \(x=e^{y}-1\) and \(x=5-y\). Set up the area with vertical slices. Use vertical slices of width \(dx\): each has height top minus bottom. Split the integral at \(x\approx 3.497\). At \(x\approx 3.497\), \(y=5-x\) meets \(y=\ln\left(x+1\right)\): \(5-x=\ln\left(x+1\right)\) when \(x\approx 3.497\) (calculator). Before \(x\approx 3.497\) the upper boundary of the region is \(y=\ln\left(x+1\right)\); after it, the upper boundary is \(y=5-x\). The lower boundary, the x-axis, \(y=0\), is the same on both sides. Because the upper boundary changes, the height of a slice, \(h(x)\), has a different formula on each side of \(x\approx 3.497\), so one integrand cannot be used on the whole interval: the integral must be split at \(x\approx 3.497\), with one integral for each piece. \(\displaystyle h(x)=\begin{cases}\ln\left(x+1\right), & 0\le x\le 3.497\\5-x, & 3.497\le x\le 5\end{cases}\) Write one integral for each piece. With horizontal slices instead, the left and right boundaries do not change, so the area could also be written as a single integral with respect to \(y\). \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{3.497}\ln\left(x+1\right)\,dx + \int_{3.497}^{5}\left(5-x\right)\,dx\) Evaluate with the calculator. Use the numerical integration feature with the intersection values at full precision. \(\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{3.497}\ln\left(x+1\right)\,dx + \int_{3.497}^{5}\left(5-x\right)\,dx\approx 4.393\)

The radius is the distance from the axis to the shell: \(r(x)=3 - x\). The height is top minus bottom: \(h(x)=2+\ln x-\left(x^{2}-1\right)\). Set up the volume. Each shell has volume \(2\pi\,r\,h\) times its thickness. \(\displaystyle V=2\pi\int_{0.050}^{1.910}\left(3 - x\right)\left(2+\ln x-\left(x^{2}-1\right)\right)\,dx\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}x + 2,&-2\le x\lt 1\\2x,&1\le x\le3\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=1\). At \(x=1\) the formula changes from \(x + 2\) to \(2x\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([-2,3]\): split the integral at \(x=1\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,dx=\int_{-2}^{1}\left(x + 2\right)\,dx+\int_{1}^{3}2x\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{1}\left(x + 2\right)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2x\right]_{-2}^{1}=\frac{9}{2}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{1}^{3}2x\,dx=\left[x^{2}\right]_{1}^{3}=8\) \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,dx=\frac{9}{2}+8=\frac{25}{2}\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}1,&-1\le x\lt 2\\4x^{2},&2\le x\le3\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=2\). At \(x=2\) the formula changes from \(1\) to \(4x^{2}\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([-1,3]\): split the integral at \(x=2\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,dx=\int_{-1}^{2}1\,dx+\int_{2}^{3}4x^{2}\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{-1}^{2}1\,dx=\left[x\right]_{-1}^{2}=3\) \(\displaystyle \int_{2}^{3}4x^{2}\,dx=\left[\frac{4x^{3}}{3}\right]_{2}^{3}=\frac{76}{3}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,dx=3+\frac{76}{3}=\frac{85}{3}\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}x + 2,&-2\le x\lt 0\\2x^{2},&0\le x\lt 2\\6 - x,&2\le x\le4\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=0\) and \(x=2\). At \(x=0\) the formula changes from \(x + 2\) to \(2x^{2}\); at \(x=2\) the formula changes from \(2x^{2}\) to \(6 - x\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([-2,4]\): split the integral at \(x=0\) and \(x=2\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx=\int_{-2}^{0}\left(x + 2\right)\,dx+\int_{0}^{2}2x^{2}\,dx+\int_{2}^{4}\left(6 - x\right)\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{0}\left(x + 2\right)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2x\right]_{-2}^{0}=2\) \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{2}2x^{2}\,dx=\left[\frac{2x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{2}=\frac{16}{3}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{2}^{4}\left(6 - x\right)\,dx=\left[-\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 6x\right]_{2}^{4}=6\) \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx=2+\frac{16}{3}+6=\frac{40}{3}\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{4}{x},&1\le x\lt 2\\x,&2\le x\le4\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{1}^{4}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=2\). At \(x=2\) the formula changes from \(\frac{4}{x}\) to \(x\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([1,4]\): split the integral at \(x=2\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{1}^{4}f(x)\,dx=\int_{1}^{2}\frac{4}{x}\,dx+\int_{2}^{4}x\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{1}^{2}\frac{4}{x}\,dx=\left[4\ln x\right]_{1}^{2}=4\ln 2-4\ln 1=4\ln 2\) \(\displaystyle \int_{2}^{4}x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{4}=6\) \(\displaystyle \int_{1}^{4}f(x)\,dx=4\ln 2+6=6 + 4\ln 2\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}\cos x,&0\le x\lt \frac{\pi}{2}\\4-2\sin x,&\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\pi\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). At \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) the formula changes from \(\cos x\) to \(4-2\sin x\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([0,\pi]\): split the integral at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\pi}f(x)\,dx=\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos x\,dx+\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(4-2\sin x\right)\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos x\,dx=\left[\sin x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=1\) \(\displaystyle \int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(4-2\sin x\right)dx=\left[4x+2\cos x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}=\left(4\pi-2\right)-2\pi=2\pi - 2\) \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\pi}f(x)\,dx=1+2\pi - 2=2\pi - 1\)

sequenceCatalog.question: No calculator The function f is defined piecewise. \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}x,&-2\le x\lt -1\\2x^{2} + 1,&-1\le x\lt 1\\6 - x,&1\le x\lt 2\\3,&2\le x\le4\end{cases}\)

parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx\).
parts.explanation: Split the integral at \(x=-1\), \(x=1\) and \(x=2\). At \(x=-1\) the formula changes from \(x\) to \(2x^{2} + 1\); at \(x=1\) the formula changes from \(2x^{2} + 1\) to \(6 - x\); at \(x=2\) the formula changes from \(6 - x\) to \(3\). Each formula describes \(f\) only on its own interval, so no single integrand can be used on the whole interval \([-2,4]\): split the integral at \(x=-1\), \(x=1\) and \(x=2\) and integrate each branch only on its own interval. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx=\int_{-2}^{-1}x\,dx+\int_{-1}^{1}\left(2x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx+\int_{1}^{2}\left(6 - x\right)\,dx+\int_{2}^{4}3\,dx\) Evaluate each integral and add. \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{-1}x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{-2}^{-1}=-\frac{3}{2}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{-1}^{1}\left(2x^{2} + 1\right)\,dx=\left[\frac{2x^{3}}{3} + x\right]_{-1}^{1}=\frac{10}{3}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{1}^{2}\left(6 - x\right)\,dx=\left[-\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 6x\right]_{1}^{2}=\frac{9}{2}\) \(\displaystyle \int_{2}^{4}3\,dx=\left[3x\right]_{2}^{4}=6\) \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,dx=\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{9}{2}+6=\frac{37}{3}\)
